_note: THE MAN IN THE OTHER SIDE OF THE GARAGE.
The only driver on the grid with the same car, the same team and the same
information - which is why a team-mate comparison is the one measurement
in this sport that nobody can argue with, and why it is the first number
AVAILABLE ONLY WHERE THE GRID IS TEAM-NAMED (the Formula One mods), where
rF2 reports the constructor as the CarClass. Everywhere else the entrant
is only in the result file and these pools are simply never offered - see
{a} is the player, {b} is the team-mate, {gap} carries its own units.
No determiner before a slot (LAW 13); every line stands alone (LAW 14);
no two open on the same four words.

mate_ahead.t: {a} is ahead of his own team-mate, and that is the comparison that counts in this sport.
Same car, same team, same tyres - and {gap} of it is {a}.
In the other side of that garage, {b} is looking at a timing screen he does not like.
{a} leads {b} on the road, and inside a team that is the only league table anybody reads.
Nobody in that team can explain away {gap}. It is the same car.

mate_behind.t: {b} has {gap} on his team-mate, and {a} will know exactly what that number means.
The other car is {gap} up the road, and it is the same machinery.
{a} is losing this one where it hurts most - to the man in his own garage.
Being beaten by anybody is racing. Being beaten by {b} is a conversation on Monday.
Every driver on this grid has an excuse available except the one racing his own team-mate.

mate_pass.t: And that is his own team-mate! {a} goes past {b}, and the garage will have gone very quiet.
Team-mate on team-mate - {a} takes it from {b}, and nobody on that pit wall enjoyed watching it.
There is no harder pass to make and none that counts for more. {a} is through on {b}.
{a} has done it to the other car. Same team, same equipment, and he has taken the place.
That is the one the team did not want to see. {a} past {b}, on the road, in front of everybody.

mate_passed.t: {b} takes the place off his own team-mate, and {a} has just lost the argument that matters.
The other car is through. {b} past {a}, and that will be a long evening.
Team orders will not come into it - {b} has simply gone past {a} and taken the place.
That is {a} being beaten by the same car he drives, which is the one result nobody can spin.

mate_quali_up.t: {a} out-qualifies {b}, and inside that team it is the only number anybody will discuss.
On the sheet it is {a} ahead of his own team-mate by {gap}.
Same car, one lap, and {a} has found {gap} more of it than {b}.
{b} is behind the other car, and there is nowhere in a garage to hide from that.

mate_quali_down.t: {b} has the better of it on the sheet - {gap} up on his own team-mate.
{a} is behind the other car by {gap}, and that is the comparison his engineers will start with.
One lap, same machinery, and {gap} of it belongs to {b}.
That is the wrong side of a team-mate comparison for {a}, and he will know it before the lap is over.

mate_record.t: Against his own team-mate this season it is {n} to {m} in qualifying, and that is the number the paddock actually reads.
The head-to-head with {b} stands at {n}-{m} on Saturdays. Same car, and no way to argue with it.
{n}-{m} to {a} in qualifying against the other car. Whatever else this season is, that part is settled.
On the sheet across the season it is {n} against {m} between these two, and only one of them enjoys quoting it.
Team-mate qualifying record: {n}-{m}. It is the first thing anybody in that garage looks up.

mate_record_races.t: Across the races it is {n} finishes to {m} between {a} and his own team-mate.
{a} has finished ahead of {b} {n} times this season, to {m} the other way.
On Sundays the two of them stand at {n}-{m}, and Sundays are the ones that pay.
The race head-to-head reads {n}-{m}. That is a season's worth of the same car, driven two ways.
